identity.title: EmbodiedSAM: Online Segment Any 3D Thing in Real Time

problem.claim: Enable online, real-time, fine-grained, generalized 3D instance segmentation for embodied agents using streaming RGB-D input, despite unavailable future frames and repeated observations requiring cross-frame matching.

gap.claim: Existing VFM-assisted 3D perception methods are mostly offline or too slow for practical embodied tasks, while limited high-quality 3D data makes direct 3D training infeasible.

contributions.claim: A geometric-aware query lifting module converts SAM-generated 2D masks into 3D-aware queries, followed by iterative refinement with a dual-level query decoder.
A query-based 3D mask representation supports efficient cross-view similarity computation through matrix operations for real-time inference.
An online SAM-assisted pipeline transfers 2D masks to fine-grained 3D point-cloud shapes for real-time 3D instance segmentation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present geometric-aware query lifting and dual-level query decoding as their approach to online real-time 3D instance segmentation with SAM.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance among online 3D perception models on ScanNet, ScanNet200, SceneNN, and 3RScan, and report substantially exceeding offline VFM-assisted 3D instance-segmentation methods.
The authors report strong generalization in several zero-shot dataset-transfer experiments and potential for data-efficient use.

narrative_sequence.summary: Embodied agents need simultaneous scene understanding and exploration, but high-quality 3D data is limited.
VFM assistance is promising, yet existing methods are commonly offline or too slow for embodied deployment.
Online RGB-D processing must operate without future frames and match instances across observations.
The method lifts SAM masks into 3D-aware queries, refines them, and uses efficient cross-view similarity computation.
Experiments report strong online performance, zero-shot transfer, and data-efficient potential.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly links streaming constraints and repeated observations to architectural choices: 3D-aware queries, iterative refinement, and efficient matrix-based matching.

lessons.interpretation: A compelling method narrative can map each deployment constraint to a corresponding design mechanism.
lessons.application: When presenting a real-time perception method, state the operational bottleneck first and identify the module or computation intended to address it.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the main contribution is theoretical or when deployment constraints are not central to the work.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative metrics, runtime, hardware, baselines, or evaluation protocols for the reported comparisons.
The zero-shot transfer settings and the meaning of data-efficient potential are unspecified.
The abstract does not define the claimed real-time threshold or detail how instance matching handles difficult cases.
